<reason>Both sides were excellent, grounded, and format-compliant, fighting skillfully over the same Karikó example. A (CON) built the debate's most durable line: portability — a wrong "no" under competition is appealable through other funders, collaborators' grants, and industry, while under block grants the institution's verdict is final. B's counter ("plural gatekeepers," applying to the next institute) was answered in A4.2 with the job-search-vs-funding-channel distinction, which B never addressed in its closing. A also caught a real internal contradiction (B's opening lamented "perpetual boom-bust," then B4.1 claimed competition "has never closed anything") and partly neutralized B's best concrete answer, Mill Hill, as relocation rather than defunding ("money changed postcode"). B's closing counter on default death ("attrition, not selection") was strong but A's final synthesis absorbed it: all judges are fallible, so the question is error-correction, and only competition lets a buried idea knock on a door the burier doesn't control. A's closing turned B's own "concession" line back on it and crystallized cleanly. B stayed competitive throughout but left A's strongest route standing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 2: catching the contradiction between B's "boom-bust" complaint and "competition has never closed anything," converting B's demanded instance (Mill Hill) into "money changed postcode, it never left," and drawing the job-search-vs-funding-channel distinction that B never answered in its remaining speech.</best_rebuttal>
